big_case_rationale: Resolves an entrenched 3-2 circuit split over whether federal prisoners' First Step Act prerelease-custody claims are cognizable in habeas under 28 U.S.C. 2241, affecting thousands of federal inmates, though the Solicitor General's confession of error and unreached threshold defenses (exhaustion and 18 U.S.C. 3621(b)) point toward a narrow vacatur and remand.

semantic_claims.proposition: The Court holds that a federal prisoner's claim seeking accelerated transfer out of a prison facility into prerelease custody in a halfway house or home confinement under the First Step Act is cognizable in habeas corpus under 28 U.S.C. 2241 because it seeks release from physical imprisonment into the community—analogous to parole under Preiser v. Rodriguez, Wilkinson v. Dotson, and Jones v. Hendrix—notwithstanding the Bureau of Prisons' continuing legal custody under 18 U.S.C. 3621(a), while leaving alternative defenses including administrative exhaustion and 18 U.S.C. 3621(b)'s judicial-review bar for the Fifth Circuit on remand.

The Court confines its holding to claims seeking accelerated transfer out of a prison facility into community-based prerelease custody (a halfway house or home confinement) and declines to decide whether every claim seeking a reduction in the level of custody within prison walls is cognizable under 28 U.S.C. 2241, while also reserving for remand whether 18 U.S.C. 3621(b) precludes judicial review of federal prisoners' prerelease-custody claims and whether petitioner exhausted administrative remedies.
